steps.content: In the suffocating darkness, you're trapped as if in a bottomless bog, every movement futile.
Yet... there's warmth. A fragile, lingering comfort.
Then, a shadow flickers before you, swaying like smoke caught in a breeze. It bounces around playfully, just beyond your reach.

steps.speaker: Shadow's Voice
steps.content: So then I went "BANG—!" and they all went "UGH—!" like total losers! And then—pew pew pew pew—BAM!! Surprise attack! Wiped them out in one move! Even Horo freaked out!

steps.speaker: Shadow's Voice
steps.content: Hahaha! You seriously missed out! I had some real adventures out here! No way my letters could've done it justice, and it's definitely not because I can't spell, okay?!

steps.speaker: Shadow's Voice
steps.content: So many crazy places, so many interesting people... Bet you wouldn't even recognize me now! Not some little tagalong anymore. Me and my steel pipe? STRONG. Like, S-T-R-O-N-G, got it? Ha! Might even be tougher than you now!
Whose voice is this?
...So familiar that it brings tears to your eyes.

steps.speaker: Shadow's Voice
steps.content: But... you know, I kept thinking... Why weren't you there? All my coolest, baddest moments... and you guys just... missed it. Every single time.

steps.speaker: Shadow's Voice
steps.content: Would've been way more awesome if you'd been with me. You really should've come.

steps.speaker: Shadow's Voice
steps.content: If only you'd come with me... I was all by myself... the whole time... It's so scary...

steps.speaker: Shadow's Voice
steps.content: Help me... ${PlayerName}, help me...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Where are you...
She sobs quietly, completely unable to see you. The vision unravels, the dream tearing at the edges, filling you with panic.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Hella!
[Release the shackles]
[Wake Up, White Out, Black Shackles Flash]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Ugh!!
The nearly pitch-black shackles pierce through your palm. Waking from the dream is agony—your heart hammers against your ribs, and your breath catches in ragged gasps.
Your thoughts swim through a thick haze, and it takes a long moment before you grudgingly surface into full awareness, your surroundings slowly coming into focus—
[Scene Change] MBCC Infirmary
You're here again.

Ever since the BR-005 outbreak in late June, severe Black Ring contamination has been eating away at you. EDGE suspects Hella is trapped deep within the Black Ring at the farlands, and the Mania devouring her is now flowing directly into you through the shackles. All things considered, it's a miracle you're even conscious. You push yourself up, muscles trembling.
No one waits by your bedside. No battle reports light up your terminal. Is the front line holding? Or have they already written you off—a commander who keeps collapsing, now useless to the fight?
Groping for the receiver, you slowly dial a number.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, you're awake! How are you feeling? Do you need anything? I'll notify the doctor right away...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No need. Notify Command HQ instead... I'll be joining the strategy meeting.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...Understood.
[Command Room]

July 26, N.F. 115 13:30
MBCC Chief's Office

To prevent your contamination from spreading, the strategy meeting has moved to a remote conference. Nightingale opens the call interface. On screen, an FAC soldier stands to acknowledge you, while the others seated around the round table appear to have been deep in discussion for some time.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Chief, it's good to have you with us. Please don't push yourself too hard.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: You'll find the battle report on your terminal. We'll skip the recap to save time as we still have a long list of items to cover.
You nod. In response, an FAC report materializes on your terminal, its stark summary outlining a crisis in motion:

Mania fields are fluctuating wildly across the globe, with the concentration and number of the Tide of Ashes increasing at an alarming rate.

Making this threat tangible, Apostles of Ashes, previously only seen in farlands, are now appearing near WhiteSands in unprecedented numbers.

Multiple defense outposts have fallen. Despite FAC committing vast resources to fortify the WhiteSands perimeter, nearly 90% of shipping routes are now impassable.

DisCity's external transport is crippled, trade has ground to a halt, and contact has been lost with two satellite towns.

On paper, manpower has recovered from the BR-002 campaign over the last two years.
New recruits are cycling through intensive training before being deployed to the DisSea and Ash Frontlines for vital combat experience.

However, what concerns FAC most is the source itself—

The missing farland Black Ring, BR-005. Its anomalous activity is the engine driving these global disturbances.
And now, it's sending destabilizing ripples into even more dangerous regions...
[Present battle report with images and text]
On the other end of the line, the meeting room is thick with tension, every word of the discussion strained and heavy.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: This is no ordinary sandstorm. There are strong resonance reactions detected inside BR-000, which can only be produced by a Secondary Black Ring—<color=#fb9259>BR-005</color>... In fact, the reactions are even stronger than during the outbreak of BR-005.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Which means that missing Black Ring has either grown exponentially, or... it's right on top of us.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: We're stretched thin. The FAC is committed at WhiteSands and DisSea, with assets tied down at Broken Frontline and Ash Fortifications. Our current Hypercube reserves are barely sustainable. We cannot hold without further support.

steps.speaker: Nirvana Representative
steps.content: Paradeisos has already approved a budget increase for the FAC.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: This isn't about money! We've already lost five tide barriers in WhiteSands. What we need are dedicated anti-Mania assets. Until we neutralize the source, any repairs are just a temporary fix.
Anxiety, once sparked, spreads like wildfire. The acting representative from Nirvana also raises his voice in response.

steps.speaker: Nirvana Representative
steps.content: Our Hypercube production is already maxed out. Need I remind you that Nirvana's balance sheets are still bleeding from the last deficit? How about you get West District to put pen to paper first?

steps.speaker: Nirvana Representative
steps.content: But frankly, even if they signed today, it's too late. This is what happens when you indulge the Syndicans instead of making hard choices. You can't close the gate after the herd has already broken through.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: ...Damn it. So that's their play. They targeted the Chief because contaminating the shackles compromises every Sinner linked to them. Our most effective asset against Mania is down. Now we're forced to fight a war of attrition, burning through all the resources we have.
A moment of silence falls.

steps.speaker: Outland Affairs Officer
steps.content: We all know where the Farland Alliance stands. But Fraser... They talk a big game about peace and dialogue, but their trade with those extremist city-states hasn't slowed down for a second. Push them hard enough, and they'll likely directly funnel resources to our enemy.

steps.speaker: Outland Affairs Officer
steps.content: On top of that, we lost contact with our people stationed there a while ago. We still haven't heard a word... No one knows what happened to them.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: ...What about the <color=#fb9259>Third Observatorium</color>? Can they provide any support? The Mania outside the city falls under their monitoring jurisdiction. We need any data they have—even the smallest clue could be critical.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: The location of BR-005, its detailed properties, its connection to the Apostles... They have none of this information?
He turns to the inorganic triangle beside you, only to be met with a cold, unflinching gaze.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: ...The Third Observatorium has concluded its observations regarding BR-005. Its resources have been reassigned to other tasks.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Should you have essential requirements, you may file a formal request with the Ring Research Institute. EDGE will evaluate the petition and allocate support as they deem appropriate.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Please try your best to endure.

The soldier clenches his fists and drops into his seat. A stiff silence grips the conference room. Glasses are lifted; pages are turned. Then, the discussions resume, cycling through the usual litany: diplomatic hurdles, budget constraints, resource and personnel shortages, ineffective coordination...
As their dreary, convoluted arguments drone on, the chaotic noise of contamination echoes in your mind once more.
Look Look... What a scattered mess... Pathetic Pathetic...
...Opportunity Seize the opportunity... Hope There is hope now... Almost time...
Purge them all Change the world...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Help me...
[Snap Back to Reality] Sound Effect
A dull thud jerks you back. You find your fist on the table, your hand throbbing. On the other side of the screen, every face is turned to you, waiting.
As it happens, you do have something to say.

steps.speaker: Option
options: ...The front needs helping hands, so let me go.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I have experience dealing with the Tide of Ashes. And I was on the Euphoria operation, where we rooted out the farland spies.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The situation is critical, isn't it? So let me go.
Your words are iron-clad, ringing with resolve, but the FAC soldier doesn't dare to respond. It's another, more familiar voice that answers.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: That was an unofficial operation. While your role was only advisory, you still overstepped. Have you forgotten how they hauled you back on a stretcher?

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: In your current state, no one in their right mind would put you on the frontlines.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then I'll gather intelligence from the rear.
As you say this, you switch to an encrypted channel, excluding several participants with low clearance. You lock eyes with the city-state's spymaster, your words deliberate and sharp.

steps.speaker: Option
options: I need to see Adelaide Campbell.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Where is he being held? The 9th Agency? Paradeisos?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Is he still alive?

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: He's still alive. Why, you looking to kill him yourself? Like last time?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I want to know what he's confessed!

<size=80><color=#fb9259>BR-005 OUTBREAK
Time: June 25, N.F. 115
Location: UNKNOWN
Scale: UNKNOWN
Ground Zero: UNKNOWN</size></color>

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Everyone knows he's the one pulling the strings behind the farland attacks. He controls the Apostles of Ashes, and he's an Undergrounder—an enemy of DisCity. BR-005 was his operation. He has the answers. So why is he not being interrogated?!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You prevent me from seeing him, not letting me kill him... so what intelligence has that bought you? I thought the 9th Agency could make even stones talk!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I need answers. Where is BR-005? What happened there? And what is the truth behind this outbreak?!
She offers a silent container for your outburst, her response deliberately detached.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: All you actually care about is that little Sinner, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Option
options: She's also important to the BR-005 investigation.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: We've lost enough field operatives already. This isn't a grief counseling session. We're staring down the barrel of a potential war—one wrong move means irreversible consequences. So everyone needs to keep a cool head and remember what's actually at stake.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: Get a grip. Unless you want to flood this command center with Mania or kill the adjutant standing closest to you first?
A tremor runs through Nightingale's hand as she supports you; the contamination bleeding from your body is a palpable poison to her touch.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...I'm fine, Chief.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Ngh... Damn it...
Schorl floats over with an unhurried grace, its anti-Mania blue light scanning your body. Under its calming pulse, the corruption fades alongside your panicked emotions.
Noting the change, the spymaster allows her stern expression to soften. She rests her temple on one hand and speaks, her tone now measured and calm.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: We're now on the 52nd round of interrogations with Adelaide. Standard methods won't break him—the man's a black hole. Given half a chance, he'll turn the tables on his interrogators... and that includes you.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: So our top priority is to contain him, sever all external communications, while tracking the <color=#fb9259>enemy's intelligence network</color>.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: The 9th Agency has deployed more operatives to the farlands, but with the vast distance and all the calamities between us, not one scrap of intel is reaching DisCity in time. Meanwhile, the enemy's network remains flawless. In wartime, that kind of disadvantage is fatal.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: My suspicion? The Underground has taken over the <color=#fb9259>Mania dark web</color>. You noted that during the Black Ring incident, Adelaide seemed to be syncing precise time with an unknown party. That's our entry point. Monitor their signals, crack their encryption. And mark my words: this will be a marathon, not a sprint.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: —You've had your answers. You can leave now.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: This meeting was supposed to make conflicting departments bury the hatchet and focus on the real threat. But as it stands, you're in no position to contribute. Go back and rest up for now.
You find no words for a rebuttal. Clenching your fist in frustration, you rise and let Nightingale support you as you leave.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...You said this meeting was supposed to make conflicting departments bury the hatchet and focus on the real threat...

steps.speaker: Option
options: Then why is <color=#fb9259>that unit</color> not at this table?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The ghost unit stationed at Nirvana Port, the one whose name alone makes Outlanders hesitate... Why aren't we using them? Aren't they exactly the kind of force DisCity needs right now?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But you seem to fear them.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: ...A hungry wolf may hunt a tiger for you, but wolves bite, Chief. Be careful...
Communication is completely down. A desperate need to be on the frontlines burns within you, but once again, you are left behind.
[Scene Change] Infirmary
After thirty minutes, your condition stabilizes and Nightingale takes her leave. She has been burdened with your duties since your collapse, and the weight of command now pulls her away.
Now, you're alone in the infirmary with only Schorl for company, its scanner still relentlessly sweeping over you.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: The contamination levels are becoming increasingly volatile...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Any changes with BR-005? Could it be close already? Or did Hella—cough cough!

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Please remain calm, Chief. It is impossible for a B-Class Sinner to become a Corpseborne. If your shackles were directly tied to the Black Ring's core, like what happened with BR-002, you would have difficulty regaining consciousness, just as you did in N.F. 113.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: That said, the present circumstances remain manageable. The fact that your shackles are still intact strongly suggests that the girl is alive and has not fully become a Corruptor. Your consciousnesses are still linked. I hope that knowledge offers you some reassurance.

steps.speaker: Option
options: ...Going to the front would make me more reassured.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Correction: I hope you can find more reassurance in a safe location.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: The Black Ring has become a weapon of war, Chief. This makes you, someone who can suppress it, a strategic asset of the highest value. It is for this exact reason that the enemy targeted you with that trap, to limit your mobility. Going forward, we cannot permit you to be exposed to further unnecessary risk.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: And there is no cause for alarm. The situation still remains within projected parameters. EDGE contingency plans for this exact form of warfare have long been in place. Current events are proceeding within expected outcomes. It will be resolved.

steps.speaker: Option
options: That's not the impression I got from the meeting.

steps.content: Schorl's silence descends at the opportune moment.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...And I can't let anything happen to Hella. I can't just sit back safe and sound while she's still out there.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So if you really want me out of danger, then do something about it. Find that Black Ring. Destroy it. Get Hella back.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: But the two of you are not even remotely comparable in value.

In a fit of frustration, you grab the nearby report and swat Schorl with it. It's deeply unsatisfying—the black triangle just whirls in place like a disoriented top before steadying itself, utterly unfazed. Its scanning beam immediately locks back onto you.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Your current condition is unstable. It is acceptable to direct your frustrations toward me, but I must advise against agitating yourself to the point of self-harm. I will amend my previous statement:

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Appropriate resources are being diverted to locate your friend. Given the delicate diplomatic climate, permitting <color=#fb9259>that unit</color> to participate in operations—even covertly—is a significant accommodation of your request. This action is not without its own risks, which we have accepted to provide support.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Remember Sinner <color=#fb9259>Jasmine</color>? She possesses exceptional resistance to the side effects of wielding that "Rancor." After experimentation at the Ring Research Institute, the resulting technology has been discreetly transferred to Nirvana Port. That unit is now better equipped to control those weapons, as you wished.
Another moment of deathly stillness falls.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Your language module is completely screwed since the reboot. Just stop. I don't need your emotional support. Just cut the crap and stick to your "pragmatic" war logic.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You said it yourself—BR-005 is an anomaly, and so is Hella's situation. Your Observatorium is useless now. She and the shackles are your only real lead for intel. You'd better be praying she's still alive, because let's be honest... there's been no trace of BR-005, has there?

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: ...A remarkably logical conclusion. I must admit, it is reassuring to see you analyzing the situation with such clarity.
Just as you're about to dismiss it, you receive a message.
Scored a big win? Come on, let's celebrate.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Can I still go out? Within the city's "safe zone."

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Of course. Your mobility is permitted, provided the individual you intend to meet is deemed secure and trustworthy, or if you would allow a security detail to be notified and accompany you. After all, I have no intention to impede your freedom or be a source of your displeasure.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: What do you think, Chief?
You look at the message on your terminal. The sender is anonymous, yet the identity is clear to you both. Schorl waits for your answer.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: A prudent choice. If your trust in the other party is not absolute, then I will ensure your safety during this "appointment."
[Scene Change] MBCC Exterior

With Schorl's "discreet" help, you leave the Bureau unnoticed. Outside, night has fallen prematurely. The distant, howling Tide of Ashes seems to whip the city with a grating wind, scouring the sky of its final light. The evening air carries a distinct chill.
You spot someone waiting for you by the roadside.
[CG] Driving Scene
A familiar sight, though she's switched to yet another luxury car.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I was hoping to see you in something sharp today, and you're still wearing that? I got you those new clothes to wear, not to collect dust.
steps.female_content: I was hoping to see you in something smart today, and you're still wearing that? I got you those new clothes to wear, not to collect dust.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Does MBCC think "austerity" is a fashion statement? Don't they pay you anything?
She takes off her glasses to examine you carefully.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: What's with the face? Should be riding high after a win like that. Did the old fogies give you static?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Get in. You look like you could use another drive to clear your head.
She smiles, slipping her sunglasses from her face onto yours before turning her gaze to the black triangle hovering at your side.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: And I don't mind having a third wheel along.
That's Catherine. She once took you on a joyride like this during the Great Expo. You thought little of it then, but now... now everything has changed.
Perhaps you should now refer to her by her true title—
Commander of the Nirvana Port troop, General of the 8th DisCorps Division, <color=#fb9259>Augustus</color>.
[Enter Flashback]

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Augustus has executed multiple assaults on the FAC, including direct attacks on our two Commanders-in-Chief. That woman possesses dangerous capabilities, commands a radical faction, and has demonstrated no loyalty to our city-state. Public recognition by DisCity is, therefore, an impossibility.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: If you are considering collaboration with her... Chief, I must strongly advise utmost caution.
[Exit Flashback]
